newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares seen sideways to lower next week.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares seen sideways to lower next week.

text.p: After a lethargic drift down this week, South African shares are expected to cling to lower levels next week with the potential to slide further if poor corporate earnings reports continue to cloud the market.

However, analysts said on Friday that although a slowdown in the country's economic growth and high interest rates cut into some firms' profits, stocks remained resilient to a heavy sell-off as especially offshore investors continued to nibble.

They said the Johannesburg bourse was characteristically lacklustre in the middle of the year, and that the market was looking ahead to a cut in the key central bank lending rate, currently at 17 percent, in the second half to fire up stocks.
"I foresee rather a lacklustre, dull week with no fireworks... There is an old saying 'sell in May, and go away'," said Malcolm Chapman, general manager at Absa Asset Management.
Heavyweight industrial stock, South African Breweries Ltd, this week announced below-expectation year results which knocked more than four percent off its share price at one stage.
Half year figures from South Africa's biggest packaging firm, Nampak Ltd, also disappointed, as did chicken producer Rainbow Chicken Ltd.
"Our market has really been corporate earnings driven this week and, in terms of the index stocks, not really inspired," said James Scott, an equity dealer at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

Key corporates due to report next week are expected to show mixed fortunes. Acquisitive banking firm Investec Ltd is seen shining with a 30 percent earnings jump, but industrial group Barlow Ltd is expected to eke out only a slim 12 percent improvement, slowed by gloomier economic growth.
However, stock buying interest was seen continuing, making for fairly brisk two-way trade.

"If there is a sell-off it's just going to add value to the market, you will probably see more buying coming through then. Already the offshore guys are taking advantage of the lower levels," a share dealer said.

Analysts said consistent gains on Wall Street failed to lift shares this week, and barring any dramatic moves on the U.S. bourse, South African stocks were again seen giving it the cold shoulder, remaining lacklustre and absorbed by local factors.
Most prevalent on investors' minds was a cut in rates.

"My prediction for the market (for the rest of the year) is that it will go to sleep for a while. Then we will probably have a better fourth quarter in anticipation of rates coming down," said a portfolio manager at Coronation Asset Management.
South African Breweries said this week it was pinning hopes on a cut in interest rates this year to boost flagging private consumption expenditure and revive domestic demand.
